item.title: Emperor Cinemas shuts Ma On Shan branch amid box office slump in Hong Kong
item.description: Hong Kong movie theatre chain Emperor Cinemas has announced the closure of its Ma On Shan branch amid a wider box office slump that has plagued the city’s movie industry for years. “Thank you for your support. Emperor Cinemas (Ma On Shan) will cease operations from 12 January 2026,” the cinema operator said on social media […]

item.title: Jimmy Lai case: Paralegal, activist ask for 50% sentence cut for collusion charges
item.description: A Hong Kong activist and a paralegal have asked for a 50 per cent sentencing reduction for their collusion charges in a landmark national security case involving media mogul Jimmy Lai. Activist Andy Li and paralegal Chan Tsz-wah, who pleaded guilty in August 2021 to taking part in a conspiracy to collude with foreign forces […]

item.title: Japan vessel aims to dig deep-sea rare earths to reduce China dependence
item.description: A Japanese research vessel on Monday began a historic voyage to attempt to dig deep-sea rare earths at a depth of 6,000 metres to curb dependence on China. item.title: Media tycoon Jimmy Lai in ‘advanced years’ with multiple health problems, lawyer says in mitigation
item.description: Pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai is in his “advanced years” and suffers from hypertension, diabetes and other ailments, his barrister has told the court during a mitigation hearing. item.description: The European Union on Monday offered China an alternative to tariffs in a bitter trade dispute over the bloc’s hefty duties on Chinese-made electric cars. item.title: Hong Kong’s gov’t-funded broadcaster RTHK axes all podcasts
item.description: Hong Kong’s government-funded broadcaster has stopped publishing all of its podcasts, with dozens of shows – in English and Chinese – grinding to a halt on Spotify and RTHK’s self-hosted Podcast One platform. item.title: Japan, South Korea leaders meet as China flexes muscles
